subject: science
intro: Some reactions are reversible, meaning they can go forward (reactants to products) and backward (products to reactants) at the same time. When the forward and backward reactions happen at the same rate, the amounts of reactants and products stay steady, a state called equilibrium. Changing conditions, such as adding more reactant or changing temperature, can shift the balance to make more products or more reactants. Chemists use these shifts to get more of the product they want.

steps: In a reversible reaction, the forward and backward reactions both occur.
Equilibrium is when they happen at the same rate.
At equilibrium the amounts of reactants and products stay steady.
solution.answer: The state where the forward and backward reactions occur at the same rate, so amounts stay steady.

items.prompt: A reversible reaction is at equilibrium. You add more reactant. Which way does the balance shift, and why?

steps: Adding reactant means there is more reactant than the equilibrium balance.
The system responds by using up the extra reactant, favoring the forward reaction.
So the balance shifts toward making more products.
solution.answer: It shifts toward more products, because the added reactant is used up by the forward reaction.

items.prompt: Why do the amounts of reactants and products stay steady at equilibrium even though reactions are still happening?

steps: At equilibrium both the forward and backward reactions are occurring.
They occur at the same rate, so products form as fast as they turn back into reactants.
Because the rates are equal, the overall amounts stay steady even though reactions continue.
solution.answer: Because the forward and backward reactions happen at the same rate, so the amounts do not change even though both are occurring.

items.prompt: What does it mean for a reaction to be reversible?

steps: A reversible reaction can run both directions.
It can go forward (reactants to products) and backward (products to reactants).
solution.answer: It can go forward and backward, both reactants to products and products to reactants.

items.prompt: A chemist wants more product from a reversible reaction. Name one change in conditions that could shift the balance toward products.

steps: Shifting toward products means favoring the forward reaction.
Adding more reactant (or removing product) pushes the system to make more product.
So adding more reactant is one change that shifts the balance toward products.
solution.answer: Add more reactant (or remove product), which shifts the balance toward making more product.

items.prompt: At equilibrium, you remove some of the product as it forms. Predict the effect and explain.

steps: Removing product lowers the amount of product below the equilibrium balance.
The system responds by making more product to restore the balance, favoring the forward reaction.
So continually removing product keeps the reaction making more product.
solution.answer: The balance shifts to make more product, because removing product drives the forward reaction to replace it.
